summary_en.motivation: This study aims to assess whether physics-informed neural networks can reliably solve thermo-viscous flow problems with suction and injection.
summary_en.method: A PINN is trained by embedding the governing equations and boundary conditions into the loss function to predict velocity and temperature fields.
summary_en.result: The PINN predictions show strong agreement with the BVP4C reference solver across the studied parameter ranges.
summary_en.validation: Accuracy is assessed through comparative numerical benchmarking against a Python-based BVP4C solver.

papers.title: COSHAP: An Explainable AI Framework Integrating Conformal Prediction and SHAP for Uncertainty-Aware Consumer Segmentation
papers.abstract: Data-driven decision-making in digital marketing is often constrained by the lack of transparency and uncertainty estimation in conventional machine learning models. This study proposes COSHAP (Conformal Segmentation with Hierarchical Attribution Paths), a unified framework that integrates Conformal Prediction (CP) and SHAP to model uncertainty while enhancing interpretability in customer segmentation. Using the Online Retail II dataset, segmentation was performed based on Recency, Frequency, Monetary (RFM), Tenure, and Average Basket Size features using K-Means, which was subsequently approximated using supervised models (Random Forest, XGBoost, Naïve Bayes, and SVM). CP was applied to generate prediction sets with guaranteed statistical coverage, while SHAP analysis was extended by conditioning feature attributions on prediction set membership through Hierarchical Attribution Paths. Experimental results demonstrated that the XGBoost model achieved the highest approximation accuracy of 97.36%. At a 95% confidence level, the framework achieved empirical coverage consistent with the statistical target for the ensemble models, with an average prediction set size close to 1.0, indicating high certainty in the majority of cases. However, a subset of customers at decision boundaries yielded multi-label predictions, accurately reflecting behavioral ambiguity. SHAP analysis identified Recency and Frequency as the primary drivers of segmentation, whereas COSHAP successfully uncovered the push-pull feature dynamics that trigger prediction uncertainty. The COSHAP framework effectively transforms point-based segmentation into a reliable, calibrated, and transparent decision-support system.

papers.title: A Killer Course: Building Confidence and Communication Skills Through Performance-Assisted Learning
papers.abstract: This paper discusses a university course designed to develop students’ expressive communication skills through Performance-Assisted Learning (PAL), culminating in a collaborative filmmaking project. The course, Performance, targeted students who are often less engaged in traditional lecture-based classes, particularly student athletes, and was designed to create a student-centered, active learning environment. Building on prior experience using PAL in required English communication courses, I introduced filmmaking as a performance project to examine its impact on student engagement and expressive communication. Students completed activities such as scripted conversations and readers theater in English, and produced a short film in Japanese based on Ernest Hemingway’s “The Killers.” Classroom observations and student feedback indicated increased student motivation, participation, and confidence. The findings suggest that integrating PAL activities, including collaborative filmmaking, into university courses can promote expressive communication skills, confidence, and motivation among less engaged students.

papers.title: Machine learning-based direct carbon emission prediction of cement clinker: Process data driven
papers.abstract: The cement industry is one of the largest industrial sources of carbon emissions, and effective carbon management is essential for its low-carbon transition. However, carbon emissions in cement enterprises are still mainly quantified using formula-based accounting methods, which provide limited timeliness for process-oriented carbon management. To address this issue, this study developed an engineering-oriented machine learning framework for rapidly predicting direct carbon emissions during the cement clinker production process. Field data were collected from six 5000 t/d and two 4000 t/d new dry-process cement production lines, including 74,448 sets of process parameters and 3102 sets of raw material, fuel, and clinker quality inspection data. An initial feature set was established from three dimensions: raw meal quality, clinker calcination process, and fuel quality. A hybrid feature selection strategy combining the Maximal Information Coefficient (MIC) and Decision Tree-based Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross-Validation (DT-RFECV) was used to identify 14 key parameters. Based on these parameters, eight machine learning models were developed and evaluated using six metrics. The Bayesian Optimization-based Light Gradient Boosting Machine (BO-LightGBM) model achieved the best performance, with an RMSE of 7.64, MAE of 5.01, MAPE of 0.6069%, and R² of 0.9365 on unseen production data. By integrating process mechanisms, statistical analysis, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) -based explainability methods, the study further improved model interpretability and engineering applicability. The proposed framework provides an effective approach for rapid and accurate carbon emission prediction and offers technical support for process-oriented carbon management and cleaner production in the cement industry.
